evidence_summary: After the public hearing, CPC says that consideration of Community Board and organization recommendations led it to shrink four portions of the proposed rezoning; the related report contains the underlying positions.
The sampled item is map/date revision material and is not a distinct certified CPC report in the official C-report universe.
The applicant accepted CEQR conditions and project modifications under a conditional negative declaration; the report does not attribute them to local political opposition or demands.

CB16 unanimously approved with park-replacement stipulations, and CPC records matching HPD commitments. The report does not establish whether the commitments were created by the CB request or predated it as CEQR modifications.

The proposal fell from 44 to 39 stories before certification and to 37 stories after the CPC hearing; the only stated opponent was Con Edison, and the report does not attribute either reduction to a local community actor.

The grouped Metrotech report records 14 opponents, detailed CB2 relocation demands, expansion of the CB task force, benefits beyond legal minima, and applicant design commitments. Requested zoning modifications themselves remain non-events.

This action shares the same grouped Metrotech report as RC06. It contains the same opposition, CB task-force response, relocation commitments, and design changes and must not be counted as an independent narrative.
CB12 disapproved and proposed alternatives. The FEIS changed in response to an unidentified hearing comment, so the report does not establish that a local actor caused that response.

CB8 and the BP approved with roof-repair and lease conditions. CPC shared their concerns, and HRA assured repairs and submitted a scope report in response to CPC; the local-to-response causal chain is plausible but not stated directly.

CB3, the BP, Council members, residents, and businesses opposed the facility. After the hearings DGS eliminated multi-agency fueling, reduced agency uses and fuel capacity, added an esplanade and open space, and limited new uses to seven years in response to review concerns.

The CB and BP approved with protections for existing tenants. DGS rejected sole-source disposition and a right of first refusal under Charter rules; CPC approved while merely requesting further efforts for tenants.

CB2 approved with four conditions. CPC reports a church commitment to fencing and an applicant meeting with Landmarks staff, while rejecting or only urging the community-room, traffic, and litter requests.

Local actors raised traffic and bus-routing objections and DOT continued studies and consultation. The report does not explicitly state that those procedural steps were caused by a specific local request.

The CB vote included seven no votes and the BP approved with conditions. Additional traffic analyses were undertaken at the community and BP's request, and CPC imposed tree replacement and mitigation conditions; the related lead report contains fuller testimony.
CB6 and the BP disapproved. The report states that, in response to these concerns, the applicants revised the applications to remove UN-occupied office space from the proposed disposition.
CB13 approved 31-0 after work with the church and neighbors. In response to parking and landscaping comments, the applicant documented leased parking and promised fences and bushes.

The East New York lead report records extensive opposition and affordability demands. CPC says these concerns led to the neighborhood plan and anti-displacement resources, but it rejected a requested anti-harassment district and approved the rezoning.

The lead East New York report documents displacement concerns, permanent-affordability demands, and anti-displacement programs explicitly framed as responses, while rejecting some central community demands and approving the plan.
After CB5 objections, and at CPC's request, the applicant amended the design to provide a 30-foot residential rear yard; CB5 then held a second hearing and approved the modified application.

The report records 129 opponents and organized objections. After the CPC hearing the applicant removed the tallest tower, reduced height and units, expanded open space, and added lower-income units, but the report does not explicitly attribute those changes to a particular local actor.

CB1 disapproved and the BP imposed detailed conditions. The report attributes the building reduction to Landmarks Commission review, not those local demands; CPC treated museum commitments as outside land-use scope and approved with other affordability and environmental conditions.
